The above observed changes in the size of objects are termed as thermal expansion. 10.2 Thermal expansion In the first demonstration, the size of the ball has been changed due to the application of heat. Also, in the second demonstration, the size of the vessel as well as that of the liquid has been changed due to the application of heat. These two demonstrations prove that when heat is given to a body, not only its temperature rises but its size also increases. When heat is applied to a body, the kinetic energy of its molecules increases. An increase in kinetic energy causes an increase in the amplitude of molecular vibration as well as an increase in molecular velocity. That is molecules move far apart giving greater intermolecular gap. As a result, the size of the body increases and it occupies more space than before. This increase in the size of a body due to the application of heat is called thermal expansion.

Under the application of heat, the length of a linear body, like a metallic wire or a rod, increases. This phenomenon is referred to as the linear expansion of the body. Thus, the change in linear dimension when subjected to heat is called the linear expansion of the material. Linear expansion can be observed by measuring the change in diameter of a circular plate or the change in length of a rod or wire, etc.
Suppose a metallic rod of length l1 at temperature 1 is heated up to the temperature of 2 so that its length becomes l2 due to thermal expansion as shown in figure 10.5.
It is observed that change in length (l2 – l1) is; i. directly proportional to the original length of the rod. i.e. (l2 – l1) l1
ii. directly proportional to the difference in temperature i.e.( l2 – l1)l1 (2 – 1) . . . (2)
Change in length or,  = original length  change in temperature
Where,  is the proportionality constant, and it is known as the linear expansivity of the rod.
If l1 = 1 unit of length and (2 – 1) = 1 unit of temperature then, from equation (3),  = l2 – l1.
Therefore, the coefficient of linear expansion or linear expansivity ()of a solid is defined
as the change in its length per unit original length per unit change in temperature. The SI unit of  is K–1. The value of  depends on the nature of the material of a body, but it does not
depend on the initial length and geometrical shapes of cross-section of the rod.
